population.note: FICTIONAL. About 43.5M US adults on an incretin (16.6% of ~262M). Cycling arithmetic: ever 23.0 − current 16.6 = 6.4 pts used and off now; ~35% of current users are restarters (5.8 pts) and ~1.6 pts of the off-now group have cycled at least once → (5.8+1.6)/23.0 ≈ 32% of ever-users have stopped and restarted. The share of starters still on therapy at one year has edged up from ~35% to ~40% as cash prices fall and orals spread. Income thirds average (21+15+14)/3 ≈ 16.7. The gap between the bottom and middle thirds is small because the bottom is subsidised (Medicaid at $245, HRSA free oral) while the middle lost employer coverage and pays cash. The gap at the top is about composition, not just use: top-third users are more often on tirzepatide or retatrutide with strength training and dietitian support. Age-weighted check: 0.20×9 + 0.33×15.5 + 0.24×27 + 0.23×14.5 ≈ 16.7. 65+ rose from 9 to 14.5 under the Medicare Bridge and its CMMI successor. Pediatric figure is mostly ages 12–17. Under-12 use is still specialist-only and off-label, and upper-income children are still ~50% more likely to be prescribed. The off-drug population that never could afford it is concentrated in the uninsured above 200% FPL and in small-employer workers in states without Medicaid obesity coverage. Payer split of the 43.5M: commercial 14.0M (mostly diabetes, cardiac or OSA codes), Medicare 10.5M (3.5M on obesity codes), Medicaid 6.5M (2.5M on obesity codes), HRSA free-provision 1.2M, cash/direct 10.0M, gray/imported/compounded ~1.3M. Publicly paid = 18.2M ≈ 42% of users.

access.public_coverage: The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge (Jul 2026–Dec 2027) is succeeded by a CMMI demonstration (Jan 2028–Dec 2030) on the same terms: Medicare pays ~$245/month and the beneficiary copay is ~$50. About 3.5M beneficiaries are on obesity codes, so 3.5M × $245 × 12 ≈ $10.3B/yr gross federal. That is already above the pace of CBO's original ≥$35B 2026–2034 score, and CBO re-scored in 2028. Medicaid: 31 states cover obesity at the $245 rate, about 2.5M on obesity codes, so 2.5M × $245 × 12 ≈ $7.35B/yr, of which ~70% (≈$5.1B) is federal. HRSA Metabolic Health Access Program (from Apr 2027): free daily oral GLP-1 (Foundayo or Wegovy pill) at federally qualified health centres for uninsured adults ≤200% FPL with BMI ≥30, or ≥27 with a comorbidity. Government price $149/month; 1.2M enrolled, so 1.2M × $149 × 12 ≈ $2.15B/yr inside a $2.4B appropriation that includes clinic staffing.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: generic semaglutide $6–40/month, 60+ brands. Canada: generics ~CAD 70–100/month and a common destination for US mail-order personal importation. Brazil, Mexico, China and Türkiye have generics. Cost-plus generic injectable semaglutide is available in ~170 countries. US exclusivity still runs to ~2031–32.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Managed decline: TrumpRx/direct cash for weekly injectable semaglutide or tirzepatide is $199–245 (down from ~$350). Oral starter doses are $149, maintenance orals $149–199. Retatrutide launched at $349 cash via LillyDirect against a $1,299 list price. Wegovy list is unchanged at $1,349, and almost nobody pays it. Employer coverage for weight management fell 60% → 49% (2027) → 44% (2028, Business Group on Health). Most remaining coverage requires BMI ≥35 or a cardiometabolic comorbidity plus enrolment in a lifestyle programme. Diabetes, CV-risk and OSA codes remain broadly covered, which is now the main commercial route. Prior-authorisation coding toward diabetes and cardiac indications is a known PBM audit target. The gray market (Canadian/Indian mail order, residual compounders) is roughly 3% of users, held down by FDA import alerts and the narrowing price gap. Route: weekly injectables are ~55% of fills and daily orals ~45%. No monthly product is on the US market.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, approved Apr 2028)
GLP-1 + amylin combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema, approved Jan 2027)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: alcohol use disorder with comorbid obesity or type 2 diabetes: guideline-endorsed (ASAM/APA, Oct 2027), not FDA-labelled; Novo sNDA for semaglutide in AUD filed Aug 2028 after phase 3 readout
mainstream_offlabel_uses: alcohol use disorder without obesity (addiction-medicine clinics, low-dose oral semaglutide)
microdosing / 'metabolic health' use via telehealth by people without obesity
structured 'drug holidays' and dose-down protocols around events, travel and creative work
nicotine and gambling craving reduction (observational, anecdotal)
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. CagriSema approved Jan 2027 against placebo despite the REDEFINE-4 shortfall versus tirzepatide; uptake is modest. Retatrutide: BLA filed Feb 2027, approved Apr 2028 (14 months later), mean loss ~28%, labelled for dysesthesia and GI effects consistent with phase 3. The monthly driver is realised as a filing: Amgen filed the MariTide (monthly injectable) BLA in Mar 2028 under a priority voucher, with an FDA decision expected H1 2029. Two US weekly-to-monthly depot programmes are in phase 2. No monthly or implant product is on the US market in 2028, but payers and HRSA are already designing clinic-administered monthly pathways around it. Amycretin is in phase 3, with filing expected 2029. Survodutide phase 3 reported ~16% and was filed late 2028. Muscle-preserving adjuncts (bimagrumab combinations) are in phase 2/3. Global incretin market ~$110B (2028).

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the most common class effect and the leading cause of discontinuation. Slightly worse at retatrutide's top doses.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; Ozempic label 'not recommended in severe gastroparesis'.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid weight loss; unchanged.
No causal confirmation in longer RCT follow-up; absolute risk low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; litigation consolidated in MDL, ongoing.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ~25–30% of weight lost is lean mass. Concern is greatest in Medicare-age users, whose numbers grew ~60% in the window. Bone-density signal still at abstract and cohort level.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No label change. The CMMI Medicare model requires a documented resistance-exercise or nutrition referral, and compliance is uneven.
EMA 'very rare' label for semaglutide; no US class label.
FDA removal of the warning (Jan 2026) stands.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Now a mainstream complaint. In survey self-report, ~1 in 5 current users describe muted enjoyment and about a third have taken a deliberate drug holiday or dose-down. There is still no validated instrument in a registrational trial. The same mechanism underlies the AUD guideline endorsement.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA added an exploratory hedonic-tone measure to the semaglutide AUD and MariTide post-marketing requirements; no label language.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Trial and real-world figures still conflict. Holidays of 2–4 weeks show small regain; stops of 6+ months track the STEP-1 extension.
More observational reports, especially among low-income users on free provision without dietitian access.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None; HRSA programme guidance recommends a multivitamin.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years of continuous use; effects in adolescents; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About six years of RCT follow-up now exist, with no new signal. Cycling, which now involves ~32% of ever-users, is still unstudied in a prospective design.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Post-marketing requirements on new approvals; NIH cycling cohort funded 2028, with first data not before 2031.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit product harms (dosing errors, contamination)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New reports slowed as compounding contracted; imported-generic labelling errors are a smaller new stream.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: 503B exclusion finalised 2027; FDA import alerts on unapproved mail-order generics.

food_and_beverage.state: GLP-1 households are ~30% of US households. Snack and confectionery volumes are down another 2–4% over two years, with value partly held by price and pack-size engineering. 'Protein-first' and small-format SKUs are standard shelf architecture. Private-label high-protein lines grow fastest in discount grocers serving subsidised users.

alcohol.state: US spirits depletions are down ~4% a year for two years. Kentucky bourbon distillers paused new rickhouse construction, and two Louisville-area bottling plants cut a shift. The AUD guideline endorsement turns the heaviest-drinking decile, ~60% of volume, into a treated population. Non-alcoholic and 'occasion' premium lines grow but do not offset the decline.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat. Average check holds through premium small plates and 'half-portion' menus. Casual-dining all-you-can-eat formats close quietly, and fine dining markets tasting menus to 'holiday weekends'.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking: store closures, Torrid and DXL restructuring toward online. Mainstream retailers profit from re-sizing. 'Fitted' athletic wear as status dress grows at the top end.

fitness.state: Split market. Boutique strength studios and 'body-composition' clinics with DEXA scans and protein coaching boom in affluent metros (Scottsdale, Austin, Westchester). Budget gyms are flat, and HRSA patients get printed exercise sheets.

insurance.state: Employer weight coverage is at 44%. Pharmacy trend is moderating to ~8% as GLP-1 net prices fall and coverage narrows. PBMs push diabetes and cardiac coding audits and 'step-through-oral' rules. Some employers offer a TrumpRx cash stipend instead of coverage.

pharma.state: Lilly leads on retatrutide and Foundayo; Novo holds CagriSema, oral Wegovy and the AUD franchise; Amgen is waiting on monthly MariTide. Volume growth outpaces net-price erosion, which comes through government and PBM deals. Ex-US generics compress international revenue.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Fat is no longer a reliable class marker; composition is. A lean, visibly muscled body reads as tirzepatide-plus-trainer money. A thinner but soft, slightly gaunt body reads as 'county pill', meaning subsidised oral or cash semaglutide without the gym. Untreated obesity increasingly reads as uninsured middle income or as principled refusal.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The two-tier system has hardened. Top-third users have newer drugs, dietitians, DEXA scans and strength coaching. Bottom-third users get free or Medicaid-paid drugs at FQHCs and clinics. Middle-income workers who lost employer coverage either pay $199–245 out of pocket, cycle on and off with their budgets, or stop.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals shrink rather than disappear. 'Holiday weekends', skipping a dose before weddings, Thanksgiving and vacations so food tastes like food again, are a widely known ritual. Hosts plan menus around guests who are 'on' and 'off'.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Dating profiles in large metros commonly list status ('on, Zep', 'off', 'holidaying'). Couples negotiate synchronised drug holidays for trips and anniversaries. Advice columns treat a partner's flattened affect on-drug as an ordinary marital topic.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is treated as a dial. Since the AUD guideline endorsement, wanting a drink, a cigarette or a second plate is talked about as a dose question as much as a character question. A counter-current, mostly older evangelical and some arts communities, treats appetite as something not to be medicated.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Survey self-report (2027–28): ~20% of current users describe muted enjoyment and ~33% report at least one deliberate holiday or dose-down in the past year, often for this reason. It is commonest at the top doses of tirzepatide and retatrutide. Clinicians routinely ask about it, but there is no validated measure.
interior_life.framing: Both side effect and treatment, openly. In addiction medicine the dampening is the therapy for AUD. In primary care it is a manageable side effect. In ordinary speech, 'being flat' or 'needing a holiday' is ordinary vocabulary, not a stigma.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Workers commonly time dose-downs before pitches, performance reviews or sales quarters to 'get the edge back'. Some managers report steadier, less impulsive teams. No employer encourages or monitors use, and HR guidance treats it as private medical information.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Musicians and comedians publicly discuss going off for tours or writing periods. Nashville and Austin venues note audiences drink less and leave earlier. Intensity-seeking consumption grows: extreme-sour and spicy foods, loud immersive events, fast competitive games.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Reduced desire is a common complaint. Synchronised holidays, libido-related dose-downs and couples counselling that asks 'which of you is on' are normal in GLP-1 households.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: No measurable change in turnout or ideology. The HRSA free programme is a partisan argument ('free Foundayo' versus 'taxpayers paying for willpower'). A small cross-partisan 'appetite liberty' strand objects to state-subsidised craving suppression. Bar and VFW-hall attendance declines are noticed by local party organisers.

state.regulatory_posture: Pro-access and pro-speed for branded products: priority vouchers, retatrutide approved 14 months after filing, MariTide on priority review. Hard on compounding (503B exclusion finalised) and on mail-order importation of unapproved generics. Price is managed through negotiation, not generics.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Direct subsidy without mandate. The HRSA Metabolic Health Access Program gives free daily oral GLP-1 to ~1.2M uninsured adults ≤200% FPL ($2.4B/yr). The Medicare CMMI successor keeps the $245/$50 terms. Medicaid obesity coverage is in 31 states. No requirement to take the drug.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Coverage is conditioned on BMI, comorbidity and lifestyle-programme enrolment. HRSA requires quarterly clinic weigh-ins to continue free supply, the first adherence-linked condition on public provision. Planners are openly designing clinic-administered monthly injection pathways for when MariTide arrives.
state.workforce_or_military: No mandate. The Army quietly allows waivered enlistment of recruits who reached weight standards on-drug, provided they stay on it through basic training. The rule is controversial inside DoD.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The US-versus-world price gap ($199 vs $6–40) remains a political fact. Manufacturers trade Medicare and HRSA volume for price concessions and tariff relief. Canada tightened cross-border dispensing of generics in 2027 after US demand spiked.

events.event: HHS launches the HRSA Metabolic Health Access Program: free oral Foundayo or Wegovy pill at federally qualified health centres for uninsured adults under 200% of poverty, government price $149/month, $2.4B appropriated

Business Group on Health: share of large employers covering GLP-1s for weight management falls to 49%, with more planning to cover only diabetes and cardiac codes; several offer TrumpRx stipends instead
ASAM and APA guidelines endorse semaglutide as a second-line pharmacotherapy for alcohol use disorder in patients with obesity or type 2 diabetes; addiction clinics begin routine prescribing
CMS replaces the expiring Medicare GLP-1 Bridge with a CMMI demonstration through 2030 at $245/month and $50 copay; TrumpRx cash price for weekly injectables steps down to $199
Amgen files a BLA for MariTide, a once-monthly obesity injection, under a priority voucher; FDA decision expected first half of 2029
Gallup: 16.6% of US adults now on an incretin drug; a third of users say they have taken a deliberate 'drug holiday' in the past year, most often to restore enjoyment

open_tensions: The middle third is squeezed. Employers keep exiting while public money covers the poor and the old, and cash-pay cycling tracks household budgets. Nobody yet knows what repeated cycling does.
The AUD endorsement makes reward-dampening a therapy at the same moment a fifth of users complain of it. The FDA's decision on the semaglutide AUD sNDA will have to decide which it is in law.
MariTide's 2029 decision invites clinic-administered monthly dosing. HRSA's weigh-in rule already links free supply to compliance, and a monthly product makes adherence visible to the payer.

Public spending is running ahead of CBO's original score (~$15B/yr federal across Medicare obesity, Medicaid's federal share and HRSA). The CMMI model expires in 2030, and US exclusivity ends in 2031–32.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US; exclusivity runs to roughly 2031–32
Medicare pays ~$245/month for obesity GLP-1s with a ~$50 beneficiary copay
Oral Wegovy (25 mg) and Foundayo (orforglipron) are on the market, with oral initial doses priced at $149
Wegovy list price remains $1,349 and almost nobody pays it
India sells generic semaglutide for tens of dollars a month while US brands hold far higher prices

prose.headline: The Two Thins: Free Pills for the Poor, Trainers for the Rich, and a Middle Class Paying $199 a Month to Stay Flat
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2028, about one American adult in six is on an incretin drug. That is roughly forty-three million people, against eleven percent two years ago. Almost a quarter of adults have tried one, and a third of those have stopped and started again at least once. The drugs no longer surprise anyone. What is new is who pays and what kind of body the drug buys.

Prices fell the way Washington wanted, through negotiation rather than generics. A weekly pen of semaglutide or tirzepatide costs $199 through TrumpRx, the daily pills start at $149, and Lilly's new triple agonist, retatrutide, launched in April at $349 cash for people who want the best result on the market. The list price of Wegovy is still $1,349, and nobody pays it. In Delhi the same molecule costs less than a lunch, and Americans know that.

Employers walked away. Fewer than half of large employers still cover the drugs for weight, and most of those that do require a heart condition, diabetes or a high BMI plus a wellness programme. Diabetes and cardiac codes have become the main commercial route, and pharmacy-benefit auditors know it. At the same time the state moved in at the bottom. Medicare kept its $245 deal under a new demonstration. Thirty-one state Medicaid programmes cover obesity. Since April 2027 the uninsured poor can get a daily pill free at community health centres if they turn up for a quarterly weigh-in. About forty-two percent of all users are now on public money.

The result is that the middle third uses the drug only slightly more than the bottom third. Their experience differs, and so does what it does to their bodies. In Scottsdale and Westchester, the drug comes with a DEXA scan, a protein plan and a strength coach, and the body that results reads as money: lean, hard, deliberately built. At the clinic in East Louisville the drug comes with a printed exercise sheet. The body that results is thinner but softer, a little drawn at the temples, and people have started to call it 'county thin.' The cashier who lost her employer coverage in 2027 pays $199 when she can and stops when she can't, and her weight records which months were bad ones.

The flatness is no longer a secret. About a fifth of users say pleasure has gone muted, and a third took a 'holiday' this year: a skipped dose before a wedding, a tour, a sales quarter, an anniversary. Couples synchronise them. Dating profiles say 'on' or 'off.' Comedians go off to write. At the same time, since last October, addiction doctors prescribe semaglutide to heavy drinkers precisely because it dampens wanting. The drug's main complaint and its newest use are the same effect, and the FDA will eventually have to say so in a label.

Kentucky feels it first. Spirits volumes are falling about four percent a year, and the heaviest-drinking tenth, who were most of the business, are now partly a treated population. Two bottling plants near Louisville cut a shift. Bars close earlier. Snack aisles have been rebuilt around protein, and plus-size chains keep closing stores.

No new safety signal emerged. The old uncertainties are bigger now: muscle loss in a Medicare population that grew by half, nutrient gaps among clinic patients, and a decade of cycling that nobody designed a study for until this year. Amgen has filed for a once-monthly injection. If it is approved in 2029, a dose will be something a clinic gives you rather than something you choose each week, and the state that already weighs its free patients will know who came in.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Ray Castillo, fifty-two, works on the bottling line in Shively. His line runs four days now. Sunday is shot day, and this Sunday he leaves the pen in the butter compartment. It cost $199, his own money since the plant dropped coverage last January.

His brother Hector is retiring from thirty-one years in the rickhouse, and there's a tasting in the visitor centre, the good barrels. Ray wants to taste them.

By Tuesday the food is back. He eats a whole biscuit at the Waffle House and feels guilty, then good, then guilty again. His wife Lorna is still on her pill. The clinic gives it to her free now that she's off the books at the salon, and she has to go in to be weighed in March. She watches him eat and says nothing.

On Wednesday the visitor centre is full of men in fitted quarter-zips from corporate, arms like they're carved, ordering the half pours. Ray knows what they're on and what it costs. Hector is on nothing. He holds his glass like a man holding a bird.

The bourbon is warm, then sweet, then long. Ray had forgotten long. He has a second pour and laughs at something Hector says about the '98 flood, laughs harder than it deserves, and Hector laughs back.

In the truck Lorna says, 'You were loud.'

'I was there,' he says.

Saturday he checks the bank app, then the fridge. Fourteen pounds came off since spring, and he can feel two of them coming back. Sunday night he stands at the counter with the pen for a long time before he uses it.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The AUD guideline endorsement turns the heaviest-drinking decile, ~60% of volume, into a treated population.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism and magnitude: the guideline covers only second-line use in people with obesity or T2D, issued Oct 2027. Real AUD pharmacotherapy uptake is in the low single digits, so the top decile could not become a treated population in about 14 months, and this inflates the stated ~4%/yr spirits decline.

Magnitude: the 2026 figure of ~0.6% was of children with obesity, roughly 0.1% of all children. Reusing it as a share of all under-18s implies a ~5x jump in two years, with no mechanism given and no mention of the change.

least_plausible_claims.quote: ASAM and APA guidelines endorse semaglutide as a second-line pharmacotherapy for alcohol use disorder in patients with obesity or type 2 diabetes; addiction clinics begin routine prescribing
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: two professional bodies endorse a drug within ~17 months of a single n=108 RCT and a phase 2 oral readout, before any phase 3 or label. The same timeline has a phase 3 readout and an sNDA by Aug 2028. This is a convenient acceleration, not a shown chain.

rationale.badness: The world is a harder society with new losers, not a catastrophe. Inequality is worst: the 'county thin' versus 'trainer' bodies, a squeezed middle third that cycles with its budget, and bottom-third users on free provision with nutrient gaps and no dietitians. Autonomy is eroded by HRSA weigh-ins tied to free supply, the Army waiver requiring recruits to stay on the drug, and clinic-administered monthly dosing being designed in advance. Epistemic harm is moderate: reward blunting is common (~20%) with no validated measure, and PBM coding audits show payers gaming diagnosis codes. Weight loss and falling obesity partly offset the harm to flourishing and public health.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is visibly realised. Adoption is +5.6 to 16.6, price follows managed decline, employer coverage falls 60→49→44, AUD arrives as a guideline plus an sNDA, MariTide is a filing only, and stratification, subsidy (HRSA) and mainstream-complaint reward blunting are all present with no contradictions. mechanism: the stratification chain (employer exit, Medicaid and HRSA, flat bottom-versus-middle gap) is well shown. The AUD guideline speed and the claim that the heaviest drinkers become a treated population (claims 1 and 3) are asserted. The Army waiver and the CBO re-score are also asserted. magnitude: population figures sit inside the envelope, with ever-used 23.0 near the 23.6 cap. The payer split sums to 43.5M, the HRSA, Medicare and Medicaid dollar arithmetic checks, and the approvals follow the 12-month rule. Small gaps remain. The stated '~$15B/yr federal' is below the ~$17.5B its own figures sum to, and Medicare growth is 'about 60%' in the ledger but 'by half' in the prose. The pediatric 0.6% (claim 2) looks like a misread of a 2026 baseline defined on children with obesity.
rationale.generativity: The Ray, Lorna and Hector bottling-line story shows a drug holiday for a retirement tasting, free-pill weigh-ins, men in fitted quarter-zips ordering half pours, and a pen left in the butter compartment. The world fields add dating-profile statuses, synchronised holidays, venue and bar effects, and the 'county thin' versus DEXA split. Characters, scenes and daily-life texture are strongly implied and shown more than explained.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Novo sNDA for semaglutide in AUD filed Aug 2028 after phase 3 readout
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the starting world has only an n=108 RCT and a phase 2 oral trial for AUD, yet a phase 3 readout, an ASAM/APA guideline (Oct 2027) and an sNDA are all compressed into about two years. No phase 3 event appears in the event list.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The Army quietly allows waivered enlistment of recruits who reached weight standards on-drug, provided they stay on it through basic training.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: a DoD policy that conditions enlistment on staying on a drug appears with no driver, event or causal chain behind it. It also sits oddly with 'No mandate' and the starting world's 'workforce_or_military: None'.

least_plausible_claims.quote: 1.2M enrolled, so 1.2M × $149 × 12 ≈ $2.15B/yr inside a $2.4B appropriation that includes clinic staffing.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: a new federal programme appropriated at $2.4B and enrolling 1.2M uninsured adults at FQHCs within about 20 months of an Apr 2027 launch is asserted with no appropriation route or clinic-capacity ramp shown. The arithmetic itself is fine.

rationale.badness: This is a recognisably harder society with new losers. Squeezed middle-income workers cycle on and off with their budgets, a visible body-class marker ('county thin' versus 'DEXA lean') hardens, and about 20% of users report muted enjoyment. HRSA weigh-ins and the Army rule add mild conditioning, and cycling remains unstudied. The harms are real but moderate: weight and cardiometabolic benefits are broad, no safety signal appears, and the flatness is openly discussed, so the epistemic score is not high.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Every driver is traceable. Adoption is 16.6%, the price path is managed decline ($199 and $149), employer coverage falls 60→44, and AUD arrives as guidelines plus an sNDA. No safety signal is added, MariTide is realised as a BLA filing, HRSA is the subsidy, and mainstream_complaint and class_stratification are both vivid. mechanism: Employer retreat producing cash-paying cyclers in the middle and subsidy supporting the bottom is well shown. The AUD guideline and sNDA after a phase 3 readout, the Army enlistment rule and the fast HRSA ramp are asserted (claims 1–3), and the prose says Medicare users 'grew by half' while the JSON says ~60%. magnitude: Current use (16.6) and ever-use (23, near the 23.6 ceiling) are inside the envelope. The payer split sums to 43.5M, public share is 18.2/43.5≈42%, the cycling arithmetic closes, and Medicare, Medicaid and HRSA dollars multiply out. Minor gap: the '~$15B/yr federal' figure in open_tensions does not match the sum of the stated components (about $17.5B), so I take a small deduction.
rationale.generativity: The Ray and Lorna Castillo scene is concrete and filmable: a pen in the butter compartment, the Waffle House biscuit, the tasting with the half pours, the weigh-in in March, and the bank app against the fridge. The world fields add texture in dating-profile status labels, synchronised drug holidays, and the Louisville bottling and rickhouse detail. Class-coded bodies and the HRSA clinic scenes also imply many more scenes.

least_plausible_claims.quote: ASAM and APA guidelines endorse semaglutide as a second-line pharmacotherapy for alcohol use disorder in patients with obesity or type 2 diabetes; addiction clinics begin routine prescribing
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: The only evidence in the starting world is a Lancet RCT with n=108 and a phase 2 oral trial. Major society guidelines normally need phase 3 data, and a phase 3 readout plus sNDA by Aug 2028 is also very fast. The candidate shows no chain from phase 2 to an Oct 2027 guideline.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The Army quietly allows waivered enlistment of recruits who reached weight standards on-drug, provided they stay on it through basic training.
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: Nothing in the parent or the drivers leads to a military policy that conditions enlistment on staying on a drug. It is an invented institutional change with no cause shown, and it sits oddly beside 'No mandate'.

magnitude: The parent's 0.6% was the share of children with obesity, not of all under-18s. Reusing it as a share of all children implies roughly 440k children, about a fivefold rise in two years. No pediatric driver or mechanism is shown for that jump.

rationale.badness: The world is a recognisably harder society with new losers, not a catastrophe. Inequality is the heaviest dimension: the 'county thin' versus DEXA-and-trainer split, a middle third paying $199 and cycling with its budget, and HRSA's weigh-in condition on free supply. Autonomy and cohesion take moderate hits from synchronised drug holidays, ~20% muted enjoyment, and the Army and HRSA conditioning. Flourishing and public health are partly offset by real obesity benefits, and the harms are openly nameable (epistemic 4), though no validated measure exists.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The AUD guideline endorsement turns the heaviest-drinking decile, ~60% of volume, into a treated population.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism and magnitude: the guideline covers only second-line use in people with obesity or T2D, issued Oct 2027.
